page.layout: One page of text: decorative border at top; heading block centred; verse poem with large woodcut initial at left; signature line at right below the poem. No marginal notes. Digitiser's watermark at bottom right is excluded.

main_text.l: Mproba ma jorumqua nata est tempore primum,Babaries, nostro tempore pulsa fuit.Gracia
nata fuit: Latiæ crevere Camœnæ:Quisque sua Musas
fovit & auxit ope.Nec summi procerum, nec Regum prona
voluntasDefuit, ex illis pars quoque nostra fuit.
Orta dies fuerat: sed qua, vix orta, repente-
Altera fax oritur, nec prius orta dies.
Sol oritur, Sixtine, tuus, qua vindice rursus-
Nec tibi Phœbeam satis est decerpere laurum,
Quam Latium, vel quam Gracia docta colit:P-
Nobilior nulli lecta corona tua est.Laurum alii si-
bi quisque gerant, tibi palma parata
est.Hanc Oriens soli servat, amice, tibi.

page.notes: The first word of the poem is a large woodcut initial "I" joined to "Improba" as "Mproba"; the printed initial is ornamental, read as I. Verse lines are set as printed, with italic type throughout the poem.
